\section*{Question 4}

The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x)=\sqrt{25-x^{2}}\) for \(-5 \leq x \leq 5\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find \(f^{\prime}(x)\).
\item[(b)] Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=-3\).
\item[(c)] Let \(g\) be the function defined by \(g(x)= \begin{cases}f(x) & \text { for }-5 \leq x \leq-3 \\ x+7 & \text { for }-3<x \leq 5 .\end{cases}\)
Is \(g\) continuous at \(x=-3\) ? Use the definition of continuity to explain your answer.
\item[(d)] Find the value of \(\int_{0}^{5} x \sqrt{25-x^{2}} d x\).
\item[(a)] \(f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{1}{2}\left(25-x^{2}\right)^{-1 / 2}(-2 x)=\frac{-x}{\sqrt{25-x^{2}}}, \quad-5<x<5\)
\item[(b)] \(f^{\prime}(-3)=\frac{3}{\sqrt{25-9}}=\frac{3}{4}\)
\[
f(-3)=\sqrt{25-9}=4
\]
An equation for the tangent line is \(y=4+\frac{3}{4}(x+3)\).
\item[(c)] \(\lim _{x \rightarrow-3^{-}} g(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow-3^{-}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow-3^{-}} \sqrt{25-x^{2}}=4\)
\[
\lim _{x \rightarrow-3^{+}} g(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow-3^{+}}(x+7)=4
\]
Therefore, \(\lim _{x \rightarrow-3} g(x)=4\).
\[
g(-3)=f(-3)=4
\]
So, \(\lim _{x \rightarrow-3} g(x)=g(-3)\).
Therefore, \(g\) is continuous at \(x=-3\).
\item[(d)] Let \(u=25-x^{2} \Rightarrow d u=-2 x d x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
\int_{0}^{5} x \sqrt{25-x^{2}} d x & =-\frac{1}{2} \int_{25}^{0} \sqrt{u} d u \\
& =\left[-\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3} u^{3 / 2}\right]_{u=25}^{u=0} \\
& =-\frac{1}{3}(0-125)=\frac{125}{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
